title: His father's death and the move to Blue Island, Illinois
summary: After his father died in 1924, Moore and his brother Everett were sent to an uncle in Blue Island near Chicago, a mixed community that was strange to him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I see. Ok. What, what led up to, what brought about your leaving Arizona? Your father passed at that time; wasn't it?

Yes. In 1924 I was twelve-years-old, and my father passed away. And it was a sad ocassion, of course, to have, to have a funeral at the church where all the activities are. This happened on Fourth of July. You see in those years, there was no embalmers around, and when, when a, a body -- when somebody dies, you'll have to bury him in the, in the -- right away. So, in that way, when my father died, that's when I left Chicago --I, I don't mean Chicago. I left to go to Chicago when my uncle in Chicago said bring the two younquest boys up here and we'll send them to school. That's how I got to Chicago.
That was you, and who was the other brother?
Ah, my brother Everett who was younger than me, about six years younger. We were, we were the ones that were sent to Chicago.
Where actually was that it was -- that you were living?
Just precisely where did -- it was a little suburb, wasn't it?

Yes, it was. In South Chicago had a little town called Blue Island, and that's where we were raised there in a, right in a, right in Blue Island by the Rock Island Line right from LaSalle Street Station.
What kind of community was that? Who lived there? You know, was it a black community, white community, a mixed community, or, or what?

It was all mixed. I'll never understand how I just left the reservation and I'm not exposed to any of these scenes that I saw when I first went to school. To see a black student and a white student and a Latin student here, and we're not -- I wasn't aware of It was strange to me to, to see that. It was quite a while, a month or two, when I got used to everything there and made friends and made non-friends also too. You make friends and that other type of friends too.
